_note: General waste-awareness tips. Check your own municipality's collection rules, which vary by city.

items.title: Separate wet and dry waste at home
items.body: Keep wet waste (food scraps, peels, leaves) in one bin and dry waste (paper, plastic, metal, glass) in another. Mixed waste is hard to recycle and cannot be composted.

items.title: Handle sanitary and hazardous waste separately
items.body: Wrap used sanitary items before disposal and keep them apart from other waste. Batteries, bulbs, paint and expired medicines should not go into the normal household bin.

items.title: Give e-waste to authorised collectors
items.body: Old phones, chargers and electronics contain materials that should not be dumped or burned. Hand them to an authorised e-waste collection point or collector.

items.title: Rinse and flatten recyclables
items.body: Rinse food containers and flatten cartons and boxes before putting them in the dry waste bin. Clean recyclables are far more likely to actually be recycled.

items.title: Do not litter - carry it until you find a bin
items.body: Small pieces of litter add up to recurring hotspots. If there is no bin nearby, hold on to your waste until you find one.

items.title: Compost wet waste where you can
items.body: Composting kitchen waste at home or in your community reduces what the collection vehicles have to carry and gives you free fertiliser.

items.title: How to file a useful litter report
items.body: Place the pin exactly on the spot, choose the closest category, add a short description and a clear photo if you can. Reports are reviewed by municipal staff before action is taken.
